## Install

`shinyloadtest` is now a Node.js (20+) CLI that replaces the Java-based `shinycannon` jar. There is nothing to download or install besides Node.js. It is currently published as a pre-release, so use the `next` tag: 

```bash
npx shinyloadtest@next --help
```

Or install it globally: 

```bash
npm install -g shinyloadtest@next
shinyloadtest --help
```

Recordings and output directories use the same format as `shinycannon`, so existing `recording.log` files and `run*` folders still work. The `shinycannon` command remains as an alias for `shinyloadtest replay`. 

## Secret management 

Set the Connect API key in your terminal (note that `set` is used in windows, `export` for mac or linux). Do this in terminal (after adding your API key). 

Windows: 
```bash
set SHINYLOADTEST_CONNECT_API_KEY=<add your key here>
```

Linux / Mac: 
```bash
export SHINYLOADTEST_CONNECT_API_KEY=<add your key here>
```

Verify that it was set (note that %% is used in windows, $ in linux). 

Windows: 
```bash
echo %SHINYLOADTEST_CONNECT_API_KEY%
```

Linux / Mac:
```bash
echo $SHINYLOADTEST_CONNECT_API_KEY
```

The legacy `SHINYCANNON_CONNECT_API_KEY` name is still accepted. The same variable is used for both recording and replay. If the recording was made with an API key, playback must also use one. 

## Create "Recording" of a typical user's interaction

Test a single app that has been deployed to Connect. Use the URL from the "open solo" mode on Connect.  
 - Solo mode is important. This URL, when opened with developer options, doesn't work: `https://colorado.posit.co/rsc/connect/#/apps/bec1d4bc-2ab7-4ba3-9bd6-b9e336bf3ff9/access` but this one does: `https://colorado.posit.co/rsc/content/bec1d4bc-2ab7-4ba3-9bd6-b9e336bf3ff9/`

```bash
npx shinyloadtest@next record https://pub.current.posit.team/public/shiny-shinyloadtest/ --open
```

This starts a local proxy (default `http://127.0.0.1:8600`). Interact with the app through the proxy URL as a typical user would, then close the browser tab (or press Ctrl+C) to stop. 

This generates a recording.log file which is the "typical user interacting with the app" which we will use for load testing. 

Alternatively, we can programmatically create the recording using [shinytest2](https://rstudio.github.io/shinytest2/articles/use-application-audit.html?q=load%20test#load-testing-with-shinytest2). 

## Load testing

We will run the load test for simulating the number of simultaneous users, each time saving the results to a different folder. 

Run the load test in terminal: 

```bash
npx shinyloadtest@next replay recording.log https://pub.current.posit.team/public/shiny-shinyloadtest/ --workers 1 --loaded-duration-minutes 2 --output-dir run1 --overwrite-output
```

Change the output directory and number of workers and run it again: 

```bash
npx shinyloadtest@next replay recording.log https://pub.current.posit.team/public/shiny-shinyloadtest/ --workers 3 --loaded-duration-minutes 2 --output-dir run3 --overwrite-output
```

```bash
npx shinyloadtest@next replay recording.log https://pub.current.posit.team/public/shiny-shinyloadtest/ --workers 7 --loaded-duration-minutes 2 --output-dir run7 --overwrite-output
```

The app URL is optional. If omitted, the `target_url` stored in the recording is used. 

Note that if you are getting a bunch of latency these notes will be useful: 

 - <https://rstudio.github.io/shinyloadtest/articles/limitations-of-shinyloadtest.html>
 - <https://github.com/rstudio/shinyloadtest/issues/121>

## Analyzing the results 

Reference the documentation to understand the different charts: <https://rstudio.github.io/shinyloadtest/articles/analyzing-load-test-logs.html?q=output#report-output> 

Generate a self-contained HTML report comparing the runs: 

```bash
npx shinyloadtest@next report run1 run3 run7 --output report.html --no-open
```

Without `--output`, the report is served locally and opened in your browser. Use `--format text` (Markdown tables) or `--format json` for other output. 

Depending on your organizations security policies, it may help to open the report as a "preview" rather than in web browser (the error message will be something like "CORS restricted"). 

### Optional: analyze in R

The R package can still be used for custom analysis of the same output directories: 

```{r}
library(shinyloadtest)
library(dplyr)

df <- load_runs(
  `1 user` = "run1",
  `3 users` = "run3",
  `7 users` = "run7"
)

shinyloadtest_report(df, "report-r.html")
```
